subject: Solara Health - marketplace billing transition & procurement timeline
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@solaracare.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-28T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Moving our Redwood subscription to AWS Marketplace billing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Solara is excited about the latency improvements on image-summary workflows. Procurement wants to move billing to AWS Marketplace so we can manage spend from our existing master account. Can you outline the steps and timing to convert our current direct contract to marketplace billing? We’re targeting the start of next quarter (Apr 1) if possible.

Also, procurement asked whether any pricing changes or credits would apply during the transition. Happy to send their contact if it helps.

Best,
Daniel
Director of Infrastructure
Solara Health

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@solaracare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-29T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Moving our Redwood subscription to AWS Marketplace billing

Hi Daniel — great to hear and thanks for the timing. Quick summary below of the typical conversion path; I’ll loop in Sales Ops to confirm dates and any account-level discounts.

1) Confirm procurement intent + effective date (we need the exact AWS customer account id and preferred go-live date).
2) Redwood issues a Marketplace listing transfer worksheet (one-page) and SOW amendment — this preserves the current committed pricing for the remainder of the term.
3) Solara signs the Marketplace SaaS Resale Addendum (DocuSign) and we provision a new Marketplace subscription that maps to the same entitlements.
4) On the go-live date we suspend direct billing and switch metering to Marketplace; historical usage is not re-billed but remaining committed credits carry over per the amendment.

We typically need ~3 weeks to coordinate legal and billing for an April 1 go-live, assuming prompt signatures. Marissa/Aditya — can you confirm whether we can preserve the existing committed rate RDW-2026-834 and whether we should offer a one-time transition credit to cover any billing overlap?

Daniel — if procurement wants to engage directly, feel free to introduce them to procurements@redwood.com; I’ve attached the transfer worksheet and a draft SOW amendment.

Thanks,
Sooj
Head of Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: SO-quote_v3.pdf, aws_marketplace_onboarding_checklist.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-01-30T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Moving our Redwood subscription to AWS Marketplace billing

Sooj / Aditya — quick finance check: we can preserve the committed per-token rate through the current contract term if Solara signs the Marketplace amendment before the renewal anniversary. For conversions mid-term we usually apply an accounting lock that maps existing commitment to the marketplace subscription.

We should consider a small operational credit (one month of average spend) to reduce friction during the cutover; recommend offering that as a one-time concession tied to a firm Apr 1 start and DocuSign by Feb 12.

I’ll coordinate with Billing to prepare the transfer worksheet and provide the marketplace subscription SKU mapping.

—Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com
